description: Vanadium is a hard, silvery-grey, malleable transition metal with atomic number 23 and symbol V. The elemental metal is rarely found in nature, but once isolated artificially, an oxide layer forms that somewhat stabilizes it against further oxidation. It is an average-hard, ductile, steel-blue metal that is harder than most metals and steels.
uses: Vanadium is mainly used to produce specialty steel alloys such as high-speed tool steels and some aluminium alloys. The most important industrial vanadium compound, vanadium pentoxide, is used as a catalyst for the production of sulfuric acid. The vanadium redox battery for energy storage may be an important application in the future.
characteristics: Vanadium is ductile, malleable, and not brittle, with good resistance to corrosion and stability against alkalis and sulfuric and hydrochloric acids. It is oxidized in air at about 933 K (660 °C, 1220 °F), although an oxide passivation layer forms even at room temperature. The chemistry of vanadium is noteworthy for the accessibility of four adjacent oxidation states 2–5, and it forms compounds with a wide variety of colors.
